description:
A `rules.toml` holding only custom rules silently switches off every default rule, so a malformed label is written and `jit validate` still exits 0. Default rules become always in force, derived from the configuration registry; a missing default row means the default applies.

## Background

The default rules (`label-format`, `namespace-registry`, `namespace-unique-<ns>`, `type-hierarchy-known`, each `origin = "default"`) apply in memory when `.jit/rules.toml` is absent. Once the file exists, `reconcile_default_rules_with_config` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/default_rules.rs:191-240`) re-derives them from the registry only when the file still holds at least one default-origin row (`:195-203`); a file with none is treated as having opted out, and only its rows apply. While one default row remains, the others the registry derives are appended in memory (`:227-237`), so today removing one row changes nothing but removing all of them disables every default.

`docs/reference/labels.md` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` tell adopters to add allowed values, value patterns and required namespaces by authoring custom rules in `rules.toml`. A repository following that advice without copying the default rows loses all of them, with no finding.

Reproduction on a fresh `jit init` repository:

```bash
printf '[[rules]]\nname = "custom"\nseverity = "error"\nenforce = false\nassert = { label-value-pattern = { namespace = "priority", regex = "^(high|low)$" } }\n' > .jit/rules.toml
jit issue create --title x --description d --label BAD   # exit 0, label written
jit validate                                             # exit 0, "Repository validation passed"
jit config set validation.strictness loose               # exit 0, adds no row
jit validate --fix                                       # "No fixes needed", adds no row
```

`docs/reference/configuration.md` (`:274-283`) says the next jit-driven config write, `jit config set` or re-init, writes the matching rows through to `rules.toml`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: On a repository whose `rules.toml` holds only custom rules, a label violating `label-format` is refused or reported exactly as on a repository holding the default rows, and `jit validate` does not exit 0 over it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Default rules are always in force, derived from the configuration registry: removing a default row changes no check, and the next config write or `jit validate --fix` restores the row. A present default row keeps its policy fields: its `severity`, `enforce` and selector edits take effect as they do today, and `severity = "off"` on the row is the one way to disable that default.
- [hard] REQ-03: `docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/labels.md` state what a config write does to `rules.toml` and how a default rule is disabled (`severity = "off"` on its row; `enforce = false` only stops it blocking writes), and `jit config set` does exactly that.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test owns each of the behaviors above, on a repository built in storage the test owns.
- [hard] REQ-05: `CHANGELOG.md` records the behaviour change: a repository that disabled a default rule by deleting its row sees that rule in force again.

## Decisions

- **D-01** — Owner ruling 2026-11-04 (option A2): default rules are always in force and a missing default row means the default applies; a present default row's `severity`, `enforce` and selector edits keep working as today, and `severity = "off"` on its row disables that default. Rejected: making default rows addressability-only (A1), which would void existing policy edits.

## Notes

- Reconciliation already keeps a default row's policy fields (`default_rules.rs:211-219`), and the header `jit init` writes into `rules.toml` calls them editable; both stay. Both rule evaluators skip a rule whose severity is `off` (`crates/jit/src/validation/local.rs:239`, `validation/graph.rs:153`); `enforce = false` leaves the rule reporting, so `jit validate` still fails on an error-severity finding.
- Related: `jit validate --fix` refuses a `rules.toml` holding default rows whose schemas are absent (`captured image has no schemas/default-label-format.json`). Converting `research` needed `--fix` with custom rows first, then the full file.
- Exposure on 2026-11-01: none. gf2, mealie-fi, inflected-messages and just-in-time each hold every default row their config derives. `research` holds them since its format 3 commit `9c581bd`.
- Reachable by following the shipped docs, so this decides what validation checks for an adopter.
title: Keep default rules in force when rules.toml holds only custom rules
